title: observability: token-level KV cost/latency dashboards + tracing refinements and alert tuning
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add token-level KV cache metrics and cost/latency breakdown dashboards; refine tracing for request->kv interactions; tune alerts to reduce noisy incidents while preserving SLO visibility.
body:
Context and motivation: We've observed noisy alerts and blind spots in token-level cost/latency breakdowns and KV cache interactions during the December incident. This PR consolidates token-level metrics, improves trace continuity across request->KV boundaries, introduces a set of dashboards for cost/latency attribution per-route/model, and lands a first-pass alert tuning to reduce paging noise while keeping SLO guardrails.

Summary of changes: emits new metrics (token_kv_lookup_count, token_kv_cache_hit, token_kv_latency_ms_p50/p95, token_tokenization_cost), enriches existing token-level cost/latency metrics with route and model tags, updates tracing spans to propagate kv.request_id and parent_token_idx, adds Grafana dashboards (Token Cost/Latency Overview, KV Cache Heatmap, Route-level Cost Drilldown), and updates PagerDuty Prometheus alerting rules to use p95 windows, aggregate noisy routes into rollups and add escalation thresholds. Also includes a small migration to backfill aggregated cost counters for the last 7 days in observability-store.

Checklist: - [x] Add metric emits and tests - [x] Tracing span propagation and unit tests - [x] Dashboard JSON and folder structure - [x] Prometheus alert rules and CI lint - [x] Migration script & dry-run logs - [x] SRE review and local canary run - [x] Runbook update and post-merge backfill script

Why this approach: Token-level attribution is critical to understand per-call unit economics. Prior dashboards relied on sampled traces and left significant gaps at high QPS. By adding lightweight counters and p95 latencies with model/route tags we get cost and latency signal at scale. Tracing continuity (propagating kv.request_id and parent token index) makes it easy to debug tail-latency KV hot paths without sampling-heavy tracing. Alert tuning focuses on reducing noise (using p95 and route rollups) while preserving actionable alerts for production regressions.
commits: feat(metrics): emit token_kv_cache_hit and token_kv_lookup_count in runtime v2
feat(tracing): propagate kv.request_id and parent_token_idx across spans
refactor(metrics): add route/model tags to token-level metrics and update aggregation keys
feat(dashboards): add Token Cost/Latency Overview, KV Cache Heatmap, Route Cost Drilldown (Grafana JSON)
chore(alerts): tune prod prometheus rules, add p95 windows and rollup groups
ops(migration): backfill aggregated_cost_counters for last 7 days (dry-run logs included)
test: add unit tests for metric emission and trace propagation
docs: update runbook and observability README with dashboard links
review_thread: Diego Martinez: Nice end-to-end. Two requests: 1) can we avoid high-cardinality on model_version tag by truncating to major.minor, 2) include p50 alongside p95 for trend visibility?
Aisha Patel: Good call. Truncate model_version to major.minor in runtime emit (added transformation) and kept p50 metrics as low-cardinality rollups in aggregation layer.
Priya Khanna: Integration tests flaked on prometheus rule lint in CI; please add a stable ordering to the generated YAML so CI lint is deterministic.
Aisha Patel: Fixed YAML ordering in templating helper and added a deterministic sort to rule generation. Re-ran CI.
Liam O'Connor: Alert thresholds look reasonable. Please add rationale comments to the rule file describing why thresholds were chosen and expected false-positive rates.
Aisha Patel: Added comments above each alert rule with rationale and SLO linkage. Also included escalation window notes in PagerDuty config.
Diego Martinez: Approving after verifying local canary metrics and a small synthetic load test.
Priya Khanna: Approving. Verified trace continuity in dev canary and no significant CPU impact from additional metric emits.
Liam O'Connor: Approving. Reminder to coordinate backfill during low traffic window — ops runbook updated.
merge_outcome: Merged after three approvals. Integration test flakiness was addressed by deterministic rule generation. Migration dry-run validated and scheduled; backfill run executed post-merge during a low-traffic window.
post_merge_actions: Dashboard collected: token cost/latency overview linked in runbook
PagerDuty: updated escalation and added route rollup on-call playbook
Monitoring: 72h canary monitored for alert noisiness — no new pages
notes: This PR intentionally keeps token-level emits lightweight (incremental counters + histograms) to avoid CPU regressions. We monitored canary CPU and observed <1% increase at typical QPS. We will iterate on aggregation keys if needed to further reduce cardinality costs.
